rows: Is the object a manifesto for industrial material rather than domestic comfort?
Exposed tube, sling surfaces, bicycle/pipe logic, minimum upholstery
Does the chair float on two front supports?
U-shaped spring geometry; distinguish Stam priority, Breuer refinement, and Mies curved-tube variants
Does the object signal elite corporate modernity despite anti-ornament rhetoric?
Expensive finishing, low throne-like posture, reception-space use, flat-bar steel
Is the body treated as a machine-positioning problem?
Adjustable recline, separable base and body support, chaise as mechanism
Is "Bauhaus" being used as a style label rather than a historical claim?
Simple geometry and chrome are influence signals, not proof of Bauhaus authorship
Does the design actually suit industrial production?
Material, joint count, tooling, repeatability, and maintenance must align with the aesthetic claim
